headline: Awarded $2,595,469.00 contract to rebuild Rotary Pool; also approved $19,176.26 for Main Street traffic cameras.
summary: Staff showed a Park Story Map of Nashua's parks, which is not yet public. Members also approved a $25,000 fireworks contract amendment and a $69,268.00 portable toilet change order. Staff said the new traffic cameras do not record video or read license plates.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 22, 2026 meeting, unanimously.
Approved the user warrants as presented, unanimously.
Approved Amendment 1 to the three-year fireworks contract with Pyrotecnico Fireworks, Inc., for $25,000.00, unanimously.
Approved Change Order #7 to the portable toilet rental agreement with United Site Services, for $69,268.00, unanimously.
Approved awarding the Rotary Pool reconstruction contract to JH Spain Commercial Services, LLC, not to exceed $2,595,469.00, unanimously.
Approved the sewer service permits and fees as submitted, unanimously.
Approved the pole license petitions listed in the staff report, unanimously.
Approved buying two Gridsmart vehicle detection cameras and four performance modules from New England Traffic Solutions for $19,176.26, unanimously.
Approved unsealing the non-public personnel minutes from the October 22, 2026 meeting, unanimously.
Approved sealing the minutes of the November 19, 2026 personnel non-public meeting, 4-0 by roll call.

MEETING OF THE BOARD OF PUBLIC WORKS 
NOVEMBER 19, 2026 
MEETING MINUTES 
 
A meeting of the Board of Public Works was held on November 19, 2026 at 4:00 p.m., at the 
Division of Public Works Administration Building in the Mine Falls Conference Room, 848 West 
Hollis Street, Nashua, New Hampshire 03062.   
 
Chairman, James Donchess, Mayor, declared the meeting to order at 4:00 p.m. and called the 
roll.

 A. Motion:  To Approve Amendment 1 To The Three-Year Contract With

With Pyrotecnico Fireworks, Inc Of Jaffrey, New Hampshire For Fourth Of July Fireworks

Bryan Conant, Superintendent, Parks and Recreation 
 
Good afternoon, Superintendent of the Parks Department, Bryan Conant.  This is the same 
company that we've been using for about the last 8 years.  We're very happy with the job that 
they do, and after this, this is the last year we'll be able to extend this contract, and then we will

major, major pool new construction and renovations.  They have a very impressive portfolio, and 
I'd be happy to answer any questions on this, if there are any.

Alderman Dowd.

Mr. Conant

under the concrete?   
 
Mr. Conant

Because that's where you end up with your leaks and then you have to dig up concrete.   
 
Mr. Conant

with today's technology and the different materials that they use, Alderman Dowd I would 
imagine that these materials are going to last longer than just the PVC pipe that they were able 
to use when they made Rotary pool.   
 
Mayor Donchess 
 
Commissioner Shea.

Thank you.

Board of Public Works Meeting of November 19, 2026  Page 6 of 32 
 
Chairman, James Donchess, Mayor 
 
Item C, Commissioner Gregg.   
 
Motion by Commissioner Gregg: To Approve The Purchase Of Two Gridsmart Overhead 
360-Degree Vehicle Detection Cameras And Four Performance Modules Along Main Street 
From New England Traffic Solutions Of Glastonbury, Connecticut In The Amount Of 
$19,176.26. Funding Will Be Through The Main Street Traffic Mitigation Account.   
 
Mark Saunders, Deputy City Engineer 
 
Good evening, Mark Saunders, Deputy City Engineer.  Before you is as the commissioner 
stated, we are looking to purchase two Gridsmart cameras for Main Street, as well as the 
performance modules to help with data collection along that corridor.  And I'll happily answer 
any questions if there are any.   
 
Mayor Donchess 
 
Anyone?  Alderman O'Brien.   
 
Michael B. O'Brien, Sr., Alderman, Board of Aldermen

communities in Massachusetts where they're capturing license plates and everything.  This is a 
totally different system.   
 
Mr. Saunders 
 
Correct.   
 
Alderman O'Brien 
 
Just to it out there for John Q. Public who may not comprehend this.  No need to panic.   
 
Mr. Saunders 
 
Yes.  These cameras are strictly for traffic detection so the intersection can function.  There is 
no license plate recognition.  These cameras do not record.  They are just there to detect traffic.   
 
Alderman O'Brien 
 
Thank you.   
 
Mayor Donchess 
 
Alderman Dowd.   
 
Richard A. Dowd, Alderman, Board of Aldermen 
 
This doesn't necessarily impact this particular thing, but I understand that the Nash Casino got 
administratively approved to expand their gaming floor, and they provided the City with some
_____________________________________________________________________________________________
Board of Public Works Meeting of November 19, 2026  Page 7 of 32 
 
electronics to help the traffic on Daniel Webster Highway.  Are you aware of what that is, and 
how it's going to work?   
 
Mr. Saunders 
 
Yes, so part of that mitigation package, when development comes in, we asked them to do a 
traffic study based on the impact that they're going to exacerbate on the network that is specific.  
When they first came in, they gave us about $100,000.00 to retime D. W. Highway.  We've since 
done a post-traffic analysis, and it's working as well as it can, but we think we can squeeze a 
little more out of it, so they're going to contribute about $45,000.00, and that's going to upgrade 
the other cameras along DEW Highway to help with some synchronization through that corridor.

 A. Presentation: Park Story Map

Board of Public Works Meeting of November 19, 2026  Page 8 of 32 
 
Lauren Sullivan 
 
Nice to see everyone again.  I think the last time I talked to you all, I was showing you some 
really cool ways on how GIS was helping our paving program.  Now, I'm going to show you 
some really cool ways GIS is making our parks more accessible.   
 
Our Parks Story Map of our parks in Nashua has been a project that has been going on for a 
number of years.   
 
Mayor Donchess 
 
Move the mic closer to you.   
 
Ms. Sullivan 
 
Oh, gosh, sorry.  I hope that's better.   
 
Mayor Donchess 
 
I guess the mic wasn't catching your remarks.   
 
Ms. Sullivan 
 
Got it.  Hopefully, it's loud enough now.  So, this Park Story Map is something I've been working 
on for a number of years.  Lisa, when I first started, asked if it was something we could do, and I 
said absolutely.  I wanted to take it and make a little bit more out of it than just a story map, but 
I'll kind of circle back around to that towards the end.   
 
Nashua has over 60 parks in historical cultural sites ranging from many various sizes, little 
pocket parks to huge community parks.  A way to make them more accessible to people, as 
apart from getting out to the actual parks, is this nice little story map.  This isn't quite available to 
the public yet, so you guys are all kind of getting an exclusive first look at it.   
 
Essentially, you could just come to this site, and you'll start scrolling down.  You'll see a main 
map showing a point where all of our cultural sites and our parks exist.  A little intro paragraph, 
and you'll see a little hyperlink here, which we'll come back to at the end, and if you keep

photos of the stadium, and we went to every single park and took all of the photos that you're 
going to be seeing.  This is from our pictometry, the City's pictometry.  You can continue to 
scroll down.  It will zoom you to our next sports complex.  Again, you can click through these 
photos.  You can continue to scroll.  We'll move on to our community parks, and of course, 
Mines Falls and Greeley Park are huge parks, so we included some extra photos just so people 
can really get an idea of the beauty of these parks.  A trail map, which you can click on.  
Residents will be able to print them from here, so you don't have to have access to the internet 
when you're out on the trails.  Say that I am not necessarily looking for your traditional 
community park, though, and I'm more interested in something like a skate park.  There are 
these little tabs up here at the top, so I can just jump right to where the skate parks are in 
Nashua.  You can scroll down and see this really beautiful skate park that we have by Mines 
Falls, but maybe I'm a beginner, and that's a little intimidating for me.  I can continue to scroll
_____________________________________________________________________________________________

down to see if there are any other skate parks.  This Ash Street skate park seems to be a little 
bit more beginners speed, maybe, and that's where I'd like to go skating.   
 
Or maybe it's in the middle of the summer; I’m interested in pools.  I'd like to see some 
close-ups of our city pools.  We can see Centennial pool here; click through that.  We can then 
scroll to the next, Crown Hill, and see the area that that's in.   
 
Maybe I want to explore our cultural and historic sites.  I can zoom right to that.  We see our 
Firemen's Memorial, our Soldiers and Sailors Monument.  Continue to scroll down through all 
these really cool sites.  We see our Bicentennial that has been updated in a couple of recent 
years.  French Park after that, and I thought that it would be really cool because when I started 
this project, these parks did not look anything like they do now.  I started it before the 
renovations were completed, and I thought that it would be really nice to show residents and 
visitors the type of work that we're doing to improve our parks, so I added this Parks of the Past

renovations.  We can see Bicentennial.  You can see French Park.  They definitely don't look 
anything like they do now.  This is just a really nice kind of aesthetic way to view our parks

Now, if I wanted to view our parks with more detail, you can come back to this link at the 
beginning.  Click on that; now I've already opened it over here just in case I run into any 
problems, and it will bring us to a public viewer.  When I was out here taking these pictures of

pictures of it.  We filled out descriptions of it.  Not only so that the public can see what we have 
in our parks and be able to view it, but also so that we can use it behind the scenes if we need
